title: Service resilience sprint heuristics & owners guide
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, tactical guide for running short, cross-functional resilience sprints to bake SLOs and reliability controls into feature launches. It is intentionally lightweight — a set of heuristics, role commitments, and a short checklist teams can copy into their feature planning docs.

Scope:
- Focus: feature-level SLO adoption, canary+fallback patterns, error-budget allocation, and lightweight runbooks.
- Not in scope: org-wide SLO design (separate cadence), deep infra re-architecture (unless necessary).

High-level objectives (what success looks like):
1) Each feature launch has an SLO target, a canary plan, and an owner who will maintain the runbook for first 30 days.
2) Canary sizing and automatic rollback criteria defined before deploy.
3) Feature teams and SRE agree on error budget consumption policy and emergency escalation path.
4) Observability dashboards and alert thresholds published and validated in staging.

Who should be involved (roles & commitments):
- Feature PM: defines acceptable reliability target and business impact tiers (P0/P1/P2).
- Feature Lead / Tech Lead: implements metrics, rollout flags, and fallback hooks; owns initial canary rollouts.
- SRE buddy: helps pick SLI/SLO, confirms alert thresholds, signs off on runbook-lite.
- QE / Test eng: provides test scenarios (latency/throughput/failure injection) and automated checks.
- Observability engineer: ensures dashboard + tracing links captured and visual checks pass during canary.
- On-call rotation: designate the first-oncall for the launch window; ensure paging rules configured.

Key heuristics (practical rules of thumb):
- SLO granularity: prefer feature-level SLOs for user-facing endpoints and aggregate SLO for background jobs. Don’t create too many micro-SLOs; 2–3 per feature is enough (latency p95, success rate, error-rate by class).
- Error budget carve-outs: allocate 20–30% of team-level error budget for new feature experiments for first 30 days. If feature is high-impact (P0), carve-out should be lower (10%).
- Canary duration & size: default = 15 minutes at 5% traffic, ramp 5->25->50 over 3 steps if telemetry looks healthy. For high-risk features start with 1% for 30 minutes.
- Fast-fail thresholds: define immediate rollback conditions (critical errors > 1% of requests for 5m OR p95 latency degrades by >2x baseline). Make them actionable and measurable.
- Alert tiers: use three-tier alerts for feature launches: INFO (dashboard drift), WARN (error budget burn > 50% in 1h), PAGE (threshold crossed or customer-impacting errors).
- Fallback matrix: always document a safe fallback (flag-based disable, degrade UX path, or route to older model). Test fallback during canary.
- Runbook-lite: 1 page with quick recovery steps, rollback commands, and who to call. Keep it in the feature repo and link to ops channel.

Sprint pattern (6 sprint template — 2 week sprints):
- Sprint 0 (Prep, 1 week lightweight): align on SLO targets, pick SRE buddy, draft runbook-lite, create dashboard prototype. Milestone: SRE sign-off to proceed to implementation.
- Sprint 1 (Instrumentation): metrics + traces + test hooks in staging. Milestone: synthetic checks green.
- Sprint 2 (Canary plan & test): perform canary in staging, execute chaos scenarios, validate fallback. Milestone: canary checklist complete.
- Sprint 3 (Production canary): rolled to small % traffic with SRE observing. Milestone: 24h stable at target.
- Sprint 4 (Ramp & stabilization): increase traffic and tighten alerts, add customer-facing monitoring. Milestone: feature fully rolled and SLO entering evaluation window.
- Sprint 5 (Post-rollout review): capture incidents, refine alerts and runbook, hand off to platform for long-term SLO ownership. Milestone: runbook merged to team ops docs.

Suggested timeline (example for medium complexity feature):
- Week 0: PM + SRE alignment meeting (30m) + create JIRA epic (SRE-982).
- Weeks 1–2: instrumentation work.
- Weeks 3–4: staging canary + testing.
- Week 5: production canary.
- Week 6: ramp + stabilization.

Deliverables per phase (copyable checklist):
- SLO spec: one-pager listing SLIs, SLO target, measurement windows, and business justification.
- Canary runbook: traffic slices, ramp plan, rollback criteria, and commands.
- Observability dashboard: p95 latency, error rate by class, traffic, key traces, and synthetic check.
- Runbook-lite: 1 page with recovery steps and contact list.
- Postmortem template filled for any incident during rollout.

Operational play examples (short snippets):
- If error budget burn > 50% in 30m during canary: pause ramp, revert to previous canary snapshot, schedule immediate incident triage with SRE + Feature Lead.
- If p95 latency rises > 2x baseline and customer impact is detected: trigger PAGE, disable feature flag for 100% traffic.

Meeting cadence & communication:
- Weekly quick sync during rollout (15m): PM, Feature Lead, SRE buddy, Observability eng.
- Daily war-room (if PAGE): SRE lead + Feature Lead + one senior eng + PM. Keep notes in the feature’s doc.
- Slack channel naming convention: #launch-<team>-<feature>-ops. Link channel in the runbook.

Ownership & handoff:
- 30d ownership window: Feature team owns the runbook and monitoring for first 30 days. SRE escalates to platform if persistent high burn or unknown failure modes emerge.
- Transfer checklist for platform: documented SLO, runbook, stable dashboard, automated tests.

Metrics & dashboards to track during 30d window (minimum):
- Request success rate (by client / route)
- p95 and p99 latency
- Traffic volume and request rate
- Error budget remaining (displayed as %)
- Synthetic check pass rate

Risk log (quick capture):
- Risk: flaky instrumentation -> Mitigation: automated unit tests + preflight synthetic.
- Risk: too many micro-SLOs -> Mitigation: group similar checks and use a composite SLO.
- Risk: noisy alerts -> Mitigation: tune thresholds in staging, use alert dedup window.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm default error budget carve-out percentage with SRE leads (ask Arjun).
- Add default dashboard template to infra repo (GH issue #412).
- Decide whether background jobs should get feature-level SLOs or only infra-level SLOs.

Quick copy-paste checklist for feature epics:
[ ] PM defines SLO and business impact tier
[ ] SRE buddy assigned and initial sign-off
[ ] Metrics instrumented in staging and production
[ ] Canary runbook drafted with thresholds + rollback steps
[ ] Fallback path tested in staging
[ ] Observability dashboard created and linked in runbook
[ ] 30d ownership window and handoff plan documented

Notes & references: 
- Keep the runbook short — people read 1 page during incidents.
- Use feature flags liberally to provide deterministic rollback.
- Document where saved: feature repo -> /ops/runbook.md and link to Confluence ID above.

Immediate next steps (for Maya/Arjun):

- Create infra GH issue for dashboard template and assign to Ben.
- Drop one-pager SLO template into CONFLUENCE:RP-345 and link in new feature epics.

End of doc.

-- Maya (notes & working draft)
